children: Southeast Asia's six largest economies--Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam--are projected to grow by an average of 4.8% annually between 2026 and 2035, according to a report by Bain, DBS and Vriens & Partners. Growth will be supported by sustained foreign investment and capital formation, continued industrialization and infrastructure development. Resilient domestic consumption and favorable demographics will provide further impetus, the report says. Vietnam remains the regional growth leader, while Thailand lags behind its counterparts. Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand would be the most exposed in a pessimistic scenario, while Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam are expected to gain most under favorable conditions. Singapore remains the region's most resilient economy, supported by its safe-haven status, deep markets and fiscal buffers, the report says. (monica.gupta@wsj.com)
